name: Standing single-leg curl
cue: Stand tall; curl your heel toward your glute.
research: Standing single-leg cable curl (hamstring curl), right leg working, facing the column. Design values from the standard technique description, not a measured trial. The left leg stands (knee 4, the sole flat on the plate), both hands are on a horizontal grab bar of the column (0.3 H ahead of the stance, 0.68 H high, the elbows bent about 54 deg), the trunk 7 deg forward as one line from the hips (pelvis 5, lumbar 1, thorax 1) and the pelvis level. An ankle cuff (0.04 H in radius, 0.07 to 0.11 H above the ankle) on the right ankle carries a ring on its front; the cable runs from the low pulley (0.075 H, 0.48 H ahead of the stance and 0.07 H to the right, on a fork on the column's base) to the ring, so it pulls the ankle forward and the knee is curled against it. The working thigh stays still (hip flexion 7, about vertical, the foot hanging beside the standing foot just off the plate) while the knee goes from 5 to 100 deg: the heel travels back and up behind the body to 0.33 H high, the shank a little above level. The load is highest at the bottom and falls toward the top as the shank turns toward the cable's line: the moment arm against the cable, the sine of the angle between the shank and the cable, is 1.00 at the bottom, 0.73 mid-range and 0.16 at the top (the cable runs down to the pulley 6 deg below horizontal at the start and up to it -17 deg above horizontal at the end). Cable 1:1 to the stack. Geometry: design/cableB/sk.mjs curl.

targets.note: design values (standard technique), not a measured trial: the working thigh stays still, only the knee moves

camera.note: Research view of the leg curl is the lateral profile (az 95, el 10); az 105, el 6 turns it 10 deg toward the back, so the biceps femoris and the medial hamstrings read along the back of the working right thigh while the shank swings up behind it in profile. The column, the grab bar and the cable stand in front of the figure and stay in frame.

skinChecks.note: the standing foot stays flat on the plate
